drug_class: Dental Cavity Prevention Agent / Mineral Supplement
purpose: Sodium fluoride is used to help prevent tooth decay and cavities. It strengthens your tooth enamel, making your teeth more resistant to acids and bacteria that cause decay. It may also be used to treat sensitive teeth or low fluoride levels in the body.
how_it_works: Fluoride is a natural mineral that gets absorbed into your tooth enamel, making it harder and more resistant to acid attacks from bacteria in your mouth. It also helps repair early damage to teeth before a cavity fully forms. Think of it like a protective shield it builds up around your teeth to keep them strong.
common_side_effects: When used as directed, sodium fluoride is generally well tolerated. Some people may notice mild nausea if the gel or rinse is accidentally swallowed. With long-term high doses, white spots or streaks on teeth (called dental fluorosis) can occur, especially in children. Bone or joint pain is rare but can happen with very high doses over a long time.
warnings: Do not swallow toothpaste, gels, or rinses containing sodium fluoride — spit them out completely. Keep all fluoride products out of reach of children, as swallowing large amounts can be dangerous. Talk to your doctor or dentist before use if your child is under 6 years old. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, check with your healthcare provider before using prescription-strength fluoride. Too much fluoride over time can affect bones and teeth, so only use the amount prescribed or recommended.
typical_dosing: For cavity prevention toothpaste or gel, most adults and children over 6 use a pea-sized amount once or twice daily, brushing for two minutes and then spitting it out. Prescription-strength fluoride rinses are typically used once daily, swishing for one minute then spitting. Fluoride supplements (tablets or drops) for children are dosed based on age and local water fluoride levels — always follow your dentist or doctor's specific instructions.
